title: Appendix: Nigeria in Comparative Statistics
book_home_label: Back to GDI Country Studies: Nigeria
introduction: This appendix organizes comparable international statistics by analytical domain. It reports levels, trends, and a fixed peer comparison for Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa. The figures are descriptive evidence, not causal estimates, and international series do not replace Nigeria's official statistics for current or subnational claims.

required_coverage.rationale: Country scale, growth, urbanization, age structure, and fertility jointly determine service and employment pressure.
Aggregate growth must be read with real living-standard levels and price stability.
Revenue mobilization and debt burden constrain implementation choices.
Sector shares show the production structure behind growth and employment.
At least one harmonized distributional outcome is required, with survey-year caveats.
Unemployment alone is insufficient in a highly informal labor market.
Human-capital analysis needs both outcomes or access and fiscal effort.
Spending inputs must be paired with mortality and longevity outcomes.

required_coverage.domain: Basic services, infrastructure, and digital access
required_coverage.rationale: Electricity, water, sanitation, connectivity, and logistics are distinct implementation constraints.
Domestic access to finance and external exposure capture different development channels.
Government effectiveness cannot stand in for rule of law, accountability, stability, corruption control, or regulatory quality.

categories.title: Demography and Population Transition
categories.introduction: Population dynamics shape the scale and timing of education, employment, urban-service, and social-protection demands.

indicators.title: Total fertility rate
indicators.question: How quickly is the demographic transition proceeding?

categories.title: Macroeconomic Performance
categories.introduction: Growth rates indicate macroeconomic movement but should be interpreted with per-capita outcomes, volatility, inflation, and the actual-versus-projection boundary.

indicators.title: Real GDP growth
indicators.question: How volatile is growth relative to peers?

indicators.title: Nigeria minus peer-median growth
indicators.question: When does Nigeria outperform or underperform the fixed peer median?

categories.title: Fiscal Capacity and Constraints
categories.introduction: Revenue mobilization and public debt describe implementation capacity and fiscal exposure; WEO estimates and projections must be separated from historical observations.

indicators.title: General government revenue
indicators.question: How much revenue does general government mobilize relative to GDP?

indicators.question: How has the general-government debt burden changed?
indicators.subtitle_note: WEO series include estimates and projections; country boundaries differ

categories.title: Economic Structure and Transformation
categories.introduction: Sectoral value-added shares reveal the production structure behind aggregate growth and the challenge of diversification.

categories.title: Labor-Market Conditions
categories.introduction: Harmonized unemployment estimates permit comparison, but informality and source/model status remain central to interpretation.

indicators.title: Unemployment rate
indicators.question: How does measured labor-market slack compare with peers?

categories.title: Human Development and Digital Access
categories.introduction: Outcome and access indicators reveal constraints that aggregate growth alone cannot identify.

indicators.title: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.question: How does a core population-health outcome compare?

indicators.title: Internet use: ten-year country trends
indicators.question: How has Internet use changed in each country over the last ten years?

categories.title: Education and Human Capital
categories.introduction: Literacy, secondary access, and public education effort capture different stages of human-capital formation and should not be treated as interchangeable.

categories.title: Health Outcomes, Capacity, and Financing
categories.introduction: Health spending and service capacity are inputs; mortality and longevity are outcomes affected by access, quality, poverty, and demographic conditions.

categories.title: Water, Sanitation, and Financial Inclusion
categories.introduction: Basic household services and access to formal finance identify constraints that national averages of output or connectivity can conceal.

categories.title: Environmental Pressure
categories.introduction: Per-capita emissions provide context for the scale and composition of environmental pressure, not a complete measure of climate vulnerability.

categories.title: Trade and External-Economy Structure
categories.introduction: Trade intensity, external balances, export scale and composition, and technology content reveal both international integration and exposure to commodity, demand, and financing shocks.

indicators.title: Merchandise export concentration
indicators.question: How concentrated is the export basket relative to peers?

categories.title: Governance and Executive Organization
categories.introduction: Perception-based governance estimates and coded cabinet data are diagnostic measures. They do not directly establish administrative performance, policy quality, or causal effects.

indicators.title: Government effectiveness estimate
